solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Polished Germany gutted about defeat

indicators.note: a gutted thing has had its insides removed, leaving only the first and last letters of the country
about here means going round, so the remaining shell wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: the country's name with its middle scooped out
a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: A slick German side has been hollowed out by a heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glossy has a shiny, smooth finish, just as a polished surface does.

clue.text: With nothing to lose, lie about dive

indicators.note: to lose tells us a piece is dropped from the word for idling about

blocks.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
to lounge is to lie about lazily

explanation.surface: A footballer, with nothing to lose, lies around after taking a dive.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the O out of LOUNGE to leave LUNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body, much like a dive towards something.

clue.text: Draw with hard team using a new formation

indicators.note: a new formation rearranges the players, so the letters of the side line up differently

blocks.note: stale bread is hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager settles for a draw by sending out a tough side in a new formation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a position in which neither side can win, so the contest ends level.

clue.text: Agent wages upset garrulous commentator?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent
wages are pay

explanation.surface: A player's agent is upset over wages, as reported by a chatty pundit.
explanation.definitionFit: A yapper is someone who talks incessantly; the question mark admits that a chatty pundit is just one example.

clue.text: Evil manager leaving foremost of strikers out

indicators.note: foremost of picks the leading letter of the word that follows
out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of strikers

explanation.surface: A wicked boss leaves his best forwards out of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition also winks at Sven-Göran Eriksson, England manager in the 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the sinister hypnotist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, now names anyone who controls another for bad ends.

clue.text: SFA wanted a messy fan dressed differently

indicators.note: putting on different clothes changes the outward arrangement, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Scottish Football Association wanted an untidy supporter to change outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: SFA looks like the Scottish Football Association; it is the initials of the British slang phrase for absolutely nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet FA is the polite abbreviation of a British slang phrase meaning nothing at all.

clue.text: Northern fixtures English journalist admired

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: sporting fixtures are meets
E is the standard abbreviation for English
ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: An English sportswriter praised the northern fixture list.
explanation.walkthrough: Only MEETS and E are turned upwards; the journalist is added afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To be esteemed is to be held in high regard and respected, which is what being admired amounts to.

clue.text: Manager prevented from reaching final by this?

definitions.text: Manager prevented from reaching final by this?

indicators.note: kept from reaching the end, the word stops short of its closing letter

blocks.note: a gaffer is British slang for a boss or football manager

explanation.surface: A manager wonders whether a blunder cost his team a place in the final.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER minus its last letter gives GAFFE, and the whole clue also suggests a howler that could keep a boss's side out of a final.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is an embarrassing blunder, the sort of error that might knock a team out before a final.

clue.text: Left with free space to improve grounds

indicators.note: set free, the letters are let loose and can settle in a new order

blocks.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left
with means together with, i.e. and
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football club left with free space decides to improve its stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: To landscape land is to lay out its gardens and grounds attractively, an improvement to the setting.

clue.text: Fix to lose head with northern side in quarters?

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for fix drops its first letter
in tells us the following pair is placed inside what remains

blocks.note: to cement is to fix firmly
N is the abbreviation for northern
a camp is one side in a dispute

explanation.surface: A northern side fixes things after losing its captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' tempts as a team, but here it is a faction in a dispute; the question mark flags quarters as lodgings rather than fractions.
explanation.definitionFit: An encampment is a set of tents or huts where troops are lodged, i.e. their living quarters; the question mark flags the less usual sense.

clue.text: Nordic news on half-cut hooligan gang

indicators.note: cut in half means only the first half of the word survives

blocks.note: a firm is a gang of organised football hooligans
news read as the plural of new, each abbreviated N

explanation.surface: A news story about a drunken gang of football thugs from Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut also means tipsy, so the surface suggests drunk hooligans. Only FI of FIRM remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a native of Finland, which is often grouped with the Nordic countries of northern Europe.

clue.text: Short official’s empty head the object of some discussion

indicators.note: something short is cut off before its end, so the final letter goes
an empty thing has had its contents removed, leaving just the outer letters

blocks.note: the match official is the referee; the apostrophe s is just the possessive
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a referee who seems to have nothing between his ears.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics and philosophy, a referent is the thing a word or expression refers to, i.e. what is being talked about.

clue.text: Still thrashed 7-0!

indicators.note: something thrashed is beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the number written as a word
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A shocked report that a side was still hammered seven-nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so and still both mean nevertheless, conceding a point before going on.

clue.text: Female graduate taking Old Trafford side to heart

indicators.note: taking something to heart means holding it inside, so one piece goes in the middle of the other

blocks.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
the on side is the leg side in cricket, and Old Trafford is Manchester's Test cricket ground

explanation.surface: A woman graduate takes a Manchester United defeat very personally.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford suggests Manchester United, but it is also a cricket ground, and cricket gives the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mona is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a female in crossword fashion.

clue.text: Pole with energy in former side of Rui Costa?

indicators.note: a side of a word is one of its edges, here its first letter
in places the pole and energy inside the outer letters

blocks.note: former means old
a mast is a pole
E is the symbol for energy
the edge letter of Rui

explanation.surface: A Pole with energy plays in the position Portugal's Rui Costa used to occupy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rui Costa was a Portuguese playmaker, but Costa here is Lorenzo Costa, an Italian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painter from before about 1800, and Lorenzo Costa was one such Renaissance artist.

clue.text: Live broadcast of a nicer style of football

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: to live is to be, as in I am
taken as written

explanation.surface: A live TV transmission of a more attractive brand of football.
explanation.definitionFit: American football is the gridiron game, a code quite distinct from soccer, so the word names a type of the sport.

clue.text: Film popular side like Roy’s boys this year?

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
taken as written
Roy Hodgson's England were knocked out of Euro 2016 by Iceland

explanation.surface: A film about a popular team that, like England under Roy Hodgson, flopped this year.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside Out is the 2015 Pixar animated feature about the emotions in a girl's head, so it is a movie.

clue.text: Local wearing whitish City sports top

indicators.note: whoever is wearing something has it around them, so the pub goes inside the pale shade
to sport is to wear, so the colour word also takes the city letter inside it

blocks.note: pale means whitish
a local is a neighbourhood pub, such as an inn
C is a standard abbreviation for city

explanation.surface: A local lad wears a pale Manchester City football shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sports top' looks like a football shirt, but sports is a second wearing signal and top alone is the definition; two separate insertions are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point or peak of something, so it serves as the top.

clue.text: A home side working on sticking together

indicators.note: working suggests something in motion and being worked over, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
H is home, as in H and A on a fixture list, followed by side as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A home team is working on building its team spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the property of clinging or bonding, the act of things staying stuck to one another.

clue.text: Central midfielders sent off in costly action

indicators.note: central points to the single letter in the exact middle of the word
sent off means dismissed, so that letter is removed from the word it sits in

blocks.note: the sixth of eleven letters, at the very centre
steep prices are costly ones

explanation.surface: Two central midfielders get red cards in an expensive incident.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the E from STEEP to leave STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure or move taken towards some end, i.e. an action.

clue.text: Put away rebound finally after save

indicators.note: finally points at the very last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to store is to save
the closing letter of rebound

explanation.surface: A keeper tucks away the rebound after making a save.
explanation.definitionFit: Stored means kept in a place for later use, which is what putting something away does.

clue.text: Series of internationals for Turkey?

indicators.note: a series is a run of consecutive items, here an unbroken run of letters inside the word

blocks.note: the run of letters from third to eighth

explanation.surface: Turkey is lining up a series of international matches.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey is just one example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is a sovereign country, and every international team represents a country.

clue.text: One charged about park to secure Portugal a point

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the charged particle goes around the rest
securing something means holding it fast inside, so one letter grips the other

blocks.note: an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge
P is the map abbreviation for park
P is Portugal's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A player charged around the park to earn Portugal a point.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo an ippon is the full winning point, scored by a perfect throw or hold.

clue.text: Countering force spot opening against Spain

indicators.note: opening describes a gap appearing, with the spot slipping into it between the other two pieces

blocks.note: anti means against
a dot is a spot
E is Spain's international vehicle code, from España

explanation.surface: A side countering the opposition's force spots an opening against Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that neutralises a poison, so it is something that works to counter.

clue.text: Missile picked up by European groundsman?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: a dart is a small thrown missile
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A dart thrown on the pitch is picked up by a European groundsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: tending grounds is one skilled occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled job or occupation, and groundskeeping is one example of such work.

clue.text: Bung: loads of money kicked back

indicators.note: kicked back means sent the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: pots of money means a great deal

explanation.surface: A bribe: a large sum of money handed over as a kickback.
explanation.walkthrough: Bung looks like British slang for a bribe, which fits kickback; here it is the verb meaning to plug.
explanation.definitionFit: To bung a hole is to plug or seal it, so it means to stop it up.

clue.text: Daily that features current head of club

indicators.note: something that features an item includes it, so the current symbol sits within the cleaner

blocks.note: a daily is British for a cleaning lady who comes in each day
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A newspaper story featuring the current leader of a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Daily suggests a newspaper, but it is the cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairwoman presides over a board or committee, so she is the person heading a club.

clue.text: They press on-edge players to contain runs

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so the players take the run letter inside

blocks.note: wingers play along the touchline at the edge of the pitch
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Nervy players press forward to stop the other side running at them.
explanation.walkthrough: Press looks like football pressing; here it means squeezing wet laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wringers are mangles, machines with rollers that squeeze water out of washing by pressing it.

clue.text: Bit of a lather over restricting match levies

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the soapy word is read backwards
restricting means hemming in, so the outer letters close around the match

blocks.note: a sud is a single bubble of soapy lather
a tie is a cup match

explanation.surface: A manager gets into a bit of a lather over taxes restricting the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties are taxes charged on goods, such as customs or excise payments, so they are levies.
